title: Tess OS Advisory Connector Manifest v1
description: A local, descriptive, versioned record of one registered external-service connector (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, ...). It declares the connector's operations (with side-effect class and idempotency), env-var-NAME-only auth, provider API-version pin, error map, timeout, and trust tier. It does not grant authority, access, approval, signing, key custody, verifier registration, or policy enforcement. This schema is intentionally outside core/contracts/ and connectors/** — like adapters/** and docs/** — is never a gate or policy input; see connectors/README.md and docs/design/connectors-architecture.md §4.1/§7.1. Validated only by the offline, dependency-free harness at connectors/manifest_validator.py.

manifest_version.description: Pins this record to the v1 advisory contract.

id.description: Stable lowercase registry-key slug. Must equal the connector's registry directory name (connectors/registry/<id>/).

version.description: Semver. Bumped on ANY change to operations, auth, endpoints, error_map, or pins (§4.5).

aliases.description: Additional slugs the resolver will match exactly (never fuzzily) against a spec's how_it_works.integrations entries, in addition to `id` itself (§6.2).

base_url.description: HTTPS only — plaintext http:// is never a valid connector base_url.

base_url_override_env.description: OPTIONAL. The NAME of an env var whose value, if set, overrides base_url at call time — a disclosed escape hatch for self-hosted proxies / offline contract tests (never a secret; a URL, not a credential).

name.description: Header name. Required when kind == 'header'; must be absent when kind == 'url_path'.

scheme.description: v1 supports exactly ONE scheme: 'env'. 'vault-capability' is reserved in the design doc (§4.1/§11) but NOT implemented — any manifest declaring it fails validation until a future schema version adds real support.

env.description: Env var NAMES only — SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. A value here that is not name-shaped (contains lowercase, matches a known provider-key prefix, or otherwise looks like a real secret) FAILS validation — see manifest_validator.py's secret-value rejection.

value_prefix.description: OPTIONAL literal prefix prepended to the env var's value when building the header (e.g. 'Bearer ' for OpenAI's Authorization header). Never a secret itself — always empty or a fixed, public protocol string.

error_map.description: Provider HTTP status code (as a string key, e.g. '429') -> one of the typed error classes (§4.4). Every key must be a 3-digit HTTP status; every value must be a class this schema recognizes.

max_retries.description: v1 hard requirement: zero automatic retries (§4.3) — retrying a non-idempotent spend/write call is how you double-bill or double-post.

tier.description: A manifest's OWN trust.tier field can self-assert at most T1 (§7.2). T2 additionally requires a non-empty, dated evidence array. T3 is REJECTED unconditionally by the validator — core/policy/policy.yaml's verifier_keys ship empty and no agent may self-provision one; the honest ceiling today is T2.

$comment: Uses the same dependency-free JSON Schema subset adapters/contracts/adapter-manifest.schema.json documents (type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, pattern, $defs) as descriptive documentation; the actual offline check is the hand-rolled, symlink-safe reader at connectors/manifest_validator.py (same harness pattern as tools/adapter_manifest_validator.py), never a generic JSON-Schema engine and never spec_engine.spec_check (which validates Plan/SpecDocument/ScaffoldPlan/codegen-manifest, a disjoint contract).
